source.note: Scan without a text layer. National Senior Certificate paper (cover: NATIONAL SENIOR CERTIFICATE; running header: NSC). The PDF includes the cover (printed page 1), the instructions (page 2) and the information sheet (page 10); PDF page n = printed page n. The cover states that the question paper consists of 9 pages and 1 information sheet. Duration 3 hours as printed on the cover. Source file and hash are recorded in sources/maths/manifest.json.

extraction.method: manual transcription from 170 dpi page renders, checked at 400 dpi where needed

questions.text_md: $5x^{2}-5x+1=0$  (correct to TWO decimal places)
$3\sqrt{x}=x-4$

Solve simultaneously for $x$ and $y$:

$3x-y=2$  and  $2y+9x^{2}=-1$
If $3^{9x}=64$ and $5^{\sqrt{p}}=64$, calculate, WITHOUT the use of a calculator, the value of: $\dfrac{\left[3^{x-1}\right]^{3}}{\left(\sqrt{5}\right)^{\sqrt{p}}}$
questions.notes: Checked at 400 dpi: the denominator is $(\sqrt{5})^{\sqrt{p}}$ (radical over 5 only, with exponent $\sqrt{p}$), which is equal to $\sqrt{5^{\sqrt{p}}}$.

questions.text_md: Write down the next term of the sequence.
Determine the $n^{\text{th}}$ term of the sequence.
Calculate the $20^{\text{th}}$ term of the sequence.

Given the arithmetic sequence: $35\,;\,28\,;\,21\,;\,\ldots$

Calculate which term of the sequence will have a value of $-140$.
For which value of $n$ will the sum of the first $n$ terms of the arithmetic sequence in QUESTION 2.2 be equal to the $n^{\text{th}}$ term of the quadratic sequence in QUESTION 2.1?

questions.stem_md: A geometric series has a constant ratio of $\dfrac{1}{2}$ and a sum to infinity of $6$.

questions.text_md: Calculate the first term of the series.
Calculate the $8^{\text{th}}$ term of the series.
Given: $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{n}3(2)^{1-k}=5,8125$  Calculate the value of $n$.
If $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{20}3(2)^{1-k}=p$, write down $\displaystyle\sum_{k=1}^{20}24(2)^{-k}$ in terms of $p$.

questions.stem_md: In the diagram below, the graph of $f(x)=ax^{2}$ is drawn in the interval $x\leq 0$. The graph of $f^{-1}$ is also drawn. $\mathrm{P}(-6\,;\,-12)$ is a point on $f$ and R is a point on $f^{-1}$.

questions.text_md: Is $f^{-1}$ a function? Motivate your answer.
If R is the reflection of P in the line $y=x$, write down the coordinates of R.
Calculate the value of $a$.
Write down the equation of $f^{-1}$ in the form $y=\ldots$
Write down the domain of $f$.
Write down the asymptotes of $f$.
Sketch the graph of $f$, clearly showing all intercepts with the axes and any asymptotes.
questions.notes: No dedicated skill for sketching a hyperbola; tagged with fn.hyperbola-asymptotes and fn.intercepts.

questions.text_md: For which values of $x$ will $x\cdot f'(x)\geq 0$?

questions.stem_md: In the diagram below, A and B are the $x$-intercepts of the graph of $f(x)=x^{2}-2x-3$. A straight line, $g$, through A cuts $f$ at $\mathrm{C}(4\,;\,5)$ and the $y$-axis at $(0\,;\,1)$. M is a point on $f$ and N is a point on $g$ such that MN is parallel to the $y$-axis. MN cuts the $x$-axis at T.

questions.text_md: Show that $g(x)=x+1$.
Calculate the coordinates of A and B.
Determine the range of $f$.
Determine the length of OT if T lies on the negative $x$-axis. Show ALL your working.
Hence, write down the coordinates of N.
Determine the equation of the tangent to $f$ drawn parallel to $g$.
For which value(s) of $k$ will $f(x)=x^{2}-2x-3$ and $h(x)=x+k$ NOT intersect?

questions.stem_md: Selby decided today that he will save R$15\,000$ per quarter over the next four years. He will make the first deposit into a savings account in three months' time and he will make his last deposit at the end of four years from now.

questions.text_md: How much will Selby have at the end of four years if interest is earned at $8,8\%$ per annum, compounded quarterly?
If Selby decides to withdraw R$100\,000$ from the account at the end of three years from now, how much will he have in the account at the end of four years from now?

questions.stem_md: Tshepo takes out a home loan over $20$ years to buy a house that costs R$1\,500\,000$.

questions.text_md: Calculate the monthly instalment if interest is charged at $10,5\%$ p.a., compounded monthly.
Calculate the outstanding balance immediately after the $144^{\text{th}}$ payment was made.
Determine $f'(x)$ from first principles if it is given $f(x)=x^{2}-5$.

questions.stem_md: The graph of $g(x)=x^{3}+bx^{2}+cx+d$ is sketched below. The graph of $g$ intersects the $x$-axis at $(-5\,;\,0)$ and at P, and the $y$-axis at $(0\,;\,20)$. P and R are turning points of $g$.

questions.text_md: Show that $b=1$, $c=-16$ and $d=20$.
Calculate the coordinates of P and R.
Is the graph concave up or concave down at $(0\,;\,20)$? Show ALL your calculations.

If $g$ is a cubic function with:

* $g(3)=g'(3)=0$
* $g(0)=27$
* $g''(x)>0$ when $x<3$ and $g''(x)<0$ when $x>3$,

draw a sketch graph of $g$ indicating ALL relevant points.

questions.stem_md:
In $\triangle$ABC:

* D is a point on AB, E is a point on AC and F is a point on BC such that DECF is a parallelogram.
* $\mathrm{BF}:\mathrm{FC}=2:3$.
* The perpendicular height AG is drawn intersecting DE at H.
* $\mathrm{AG}=t$ units.
* $\mathrm{BC}=(5-t)$ units.

questions.text_md: Write down $\mathrm{AH}:\mathrm{HG}$.

Calculate $t$ if the area of the parallelogram is a maximum.
(NOTE: Area of a parallelogram $=$ base $\times$ $\perp$ height)

questions.stem_md: Calculate how many unique $5$-digit codes can be formed using the digits above, if:

questions.text_md: The digits may be repeated
The digits may not be repeated

How many unique $3$-digit codes can be formed using the above digits, if:

* Digits may be repeated
* The code is greater than $400$ but less than $600$
* The code is divisible by $5$

Given: $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A})=0,45$ ; $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{B})=y$ and $\mathrm{P}(\mathrm{A}$ or $\mathrm{B})=0,74$

Determine the value(s) of $y$ if A and B are mutually exclusive.

An organisation decided to distribute gift bags of sweets to a Grade R class at a certain school. There is a mystery gift in exactly $\dfrac{1}{4}$ of the total number of bags.

Each learner in the class may randomly select two gift bags of sweets, one after the other. The probability that a learner selects two bags of sweets with a mystery gift is $\dfrac{7}{118}$. Calculate the number of gift bags of sweets with a mystery gift inside.
questions.notes: Without-replacement probability (two successive draws). No dedicated without-replacement skill; tagged with count.counting-probability.
